headline: Tiny Mice Thrive Where Humans Cannot: Scientists Reveal Mountain Survival
meta_description: Scientists discover how Andean leaf-eared mice survive on volcano summits above 6,700 meters, using oxygen efficiently and metabolizing toxic plants.
summary_short: A new study explains how the tiny Andean leaf-eared mouse thrives on volcano summits in the Andes at elevations where most mammals—and humans—cannot survive.
body:
Scientists have cracked the biological mystery of how a small brown rodent survives in one of Earth's most hostile environments: the frozen summits of Andes volcanoes. The Andean leaf-eared mouse, a creature barely larger than a human hand, lives at elevations above 6,700 meters (22,000 feet) where oxygen is scarce, temperatures remain perpetually below freezing, and humans cannot breathe without masks and heavy insulation. A new study reveals that these remarkable animals have evolved not one but multiple genetic advantages—they use oxygen more efficiently in their muscles, generate extra body heat, and can even break down toxins in the plants they eat.

Researchers collected 167 mice from across the species' range, from sea-level deserts in northern Chile to their extreme mountain homes, then exposed highland and lowland populations to simulated high-altitude conditions in the laboratory. The highland mice showed superior oxygen metabolism and heat production compared to their lowland relatives. Even more surprising, genetic analysis revealed that these mountain mice have evolved the ability to metabolize plant toxins—an adaptation that underscores just how unforgiving their habitat truly is. As evolutionary biologist Jay Storz explained, survival at extreme elevation demands far more than coping with thin air and freezing cold; the very food available to these mice is poisonous to most other animals.

The discovery opens new questions about how other high-elevation species have adapted to extreme conditions. Researchers are now conducting comparative studies to understand whether different mountain mammals evolve similar solutions to the same challenges, or whether nature achieves survival through entirely different biological pathways in each species.
quick_facts: Lives above 6,700 meters on volcano summits in the central Andes Mountains
Highland mice use oxygen more efficiently than lowland relatives
Evolved ability to metabolize toxic plants found at high elevations
Study analyzed 167 mice from sea level to extreme mountain altitudes
